_how: Who each result is, in the site's plain voice: short dates, one line of who, a hook of at most 35 words drawn from research/figures (each story is sourced there), and a status note where a devout player should not be surprised later. 'pairs' are real links between two people, printed when a result names both.

augustine.name: Augustine of Hippo
augustine.who: Bishop of Hippo. His Confessions is the first great life story told from the inside.
augustine.hook: At sixteen he stole pears he did not even want and threw them to the pigs. Thirty years later he spent pages of his Confessions working out why.

chrysostom.name: John Chrysostom
chrysostom.who: Archbishop of Constantinople. His name means golden mouth.
chrysostom.hook: He told the rich that keeping their surplus from the poor was robbery. The empress exiled him twice, and he died on the road saying: Glory to God for all things.

tertullian.name: Tertullian
tertullian.who: The first great Christian writer in Latin, with a lawyer's mind and a fighter's temper.
tertullian.hook: He wrote a whole book urging patience. He opened it by admitting that he himself was ever sick with the heats of impatience.
tertullian.status: Late in life he joined the New Prophecy, a breakaway movement, and he is not counted a saint.

jerome.name: Jerome
jerome.who: Scholar and monk who gave the West its Latin Bible.
jerome.hook: In a fever he dreamed that Christ called him a follower of Cicero, not of Christ. He also wrote some of the angriest letters in Christian history.

clement.name: Clement of Alexandria
clement.who: Teacher in the ancient world's great city of learning.
clement.hook: He wanted Christians to read Plato without fear, and he called the whole of life a festival.

ambrose.name: Ambrose of Milan
ambrose.who: Roman governor turned bishop. He baptised Augustine.
ambrose.hook: He came to calm a riot over who should be bishop, and the crowd chose him. He fled the city by night. Eight days after his baptism he was bishop anyway.

gregory.name: Gregory the Great
gregory.who: Monk, then pope. He sent the mission that brought the faith to the English.
gregory.hook: Chosen pope in a plague year, he was about to slip away into hiding. He was seized and carried to St Peter's, and he complained for years that the job had wrecked his peace.

basil.name: Basil the Great
basil.who: Bishop who built a whole new quarter of care for the poor and the sick outside his city.
basil.hook: The emperor's prefect threatened him with exile, torture and death. Basil answered that a man who owns only rags and a few books cannot be robbed, and death would only send him to God sooner.

nazianzen.name: Gregory of Nazianzus
nazianzen.who: Poet and preacher, and Basil's best friend.
nazianzen.hook: He was made a bishop three times against his will. He resigned the greatest church in the East and asked to go home to his desert, his country life, and his God.

nyssa.name: Gregory of Nyssa
nyssa.who: Basil's younger brother, and the boldest thinker in the family.
nyssa.hook: He once forged letters from his uncle to patch up a family feud, and got caught. His brother Basil told him he was too simple to be trusted.

lactantius.name: Lactantius
lactantius.who: Latin professor who became a Christian writer, then tutor to Constantine's son.
lactantius.hook: He watched soldiers tear down the church across from the emperor's palace. He wrote that a Christian may never kill anyone, not even in war.

origen.name: Origen
origen.who: The greatest Bible scholar of the early Church.
origen.hook: As a teenager he was so set on dying with his arrested father that his mother hid all his clothes to keep him home.
origen.status: Some of his ideas were condemned three centuries after his death, and he is not counted a saint.

cyprian.name: Cyprian of Carthage
cyprian.who: Rich orator turned bishop, who died a martyr.
cyprian.hook: He hid from one persecution and led his church by letter. When the sword finally came, he said: Thanks be to God. Then he had his friends give the executioner twenty-five gold coins.

antony.name: Antony the Great
antony.who: The father of the desert monks.
antony.hook: At eighteen he heard one Gospel verse in church, walked out, and gave away his farm. He spent the next eighty years in the desert, where emperors wrote to him.

cassian.name: John Cassian
cassian.who: Monk who carried the wisdom of the Egyptian desert to the West.
cassian.hook: After years among the holiest monks of Egypt, he admitted he still lost his temper alone in his cell. At his pen. At his blunt knife. At his flint, when it would not spark.

isaac.name: Isaac the Syrian
isaac.who: Hermit and bishop, read by monks East and West to this day.
isaac.hook: Made bishop of Nineveh, he quit after five months. He wrote that a merciful heart burns with love for every creature, even the demons.

macrina.name: Macrina the Younger
macrina.who: Eldest sister of Basil and Gregory of Nyssa. Gregory called her the Teacher.
macrina.hook: When her fiancé died, she refused every other suitor. Then she talked her proud brother Basil out of his vanity, and her rich mother into sharing the servants' bread.

justin.name: Justin Martyr
justin.who: Philosopher who became the first great defender of the faith.
justin.hook: He shopped around for a philosophy and walked out on a teacher who wanted his fee up front. A stranger by the sea talked him into Christ.

irenaeus.name: Irenaeus of Lyons
irenaeus.who: Bishop who learned the faith from Polycarp, a disciple of the apostle John.
irenaeus.hook: To mock one sect's grand names for hidden cosmic powers, he invented his own: the Gourd, Utter-Emptiness, the Cucumber and the Melon.

martin.name: Martin of Tours
martin.who: Soldier turned monk and bishop, the best loved saint of Gaul.
martin.hook: As a young cavalryman he cut his cloak in half with his sword for a freezing beggar. Later he told the emperor he was Christ's soldier, and could not fight.

benedict.name: Benedict of Nursia
benedict.who: Author of the Rule that has shaped Western monks for fifteen hundred years.
benedict.hook: As a young man he lived three years in a cave. A friend lowered bread to him on a rope, with a little bell tied to it.

boethius.name: Boethius
boethius.who: Philosopher and the top civil servant of Gothic Italy.
boethius.hook: Condemned without a hearing, he wrote a book in his cell while he waited to die. In it, Philosophy walks in and throws out the Muses of self-pity.

pairs.basil|nazianzen: Basil and Gregory of Nazianzus were best friends from their student days in Athens.
pairs.basil|nyssa: Basil and Gregory of Nyssa were brothers.
pairs.nyssa|macrina: Macrina was Gregory of Nyssa's older sister. He wrote down her words.
pairs.ambrose|augustine: Ambrose baptised Augustine in Milan, at Easter in 387.
pairs.jerome|augustine: Jerome and Augustine traded sharp letters for twenty years.
pairs.jerome|origen: Jerome translated Origen and admired him, then turned against his ideas.
pairs.augustine|origen: Augustine argued against Origen's hope that everyone would be restored in the end.
pairs.cassian|augustine: Augustine's followers attacked Cassian's teaching on grace and effort.
pairs.chrysostom|cassian: Chrysostom ordained Cassian a deacon in Constantinople.
pairs.cyprian|tertullian: Jerome says Cyprian read Tertullian every day and called him the master.
pairs.gregory|benedict: Gregory the Great wrote the only early life of Benedict.
pairs.justin|irenaeus: Irenaeus read Justin and quotes him.
pairs.clement|origen: An early historian says Origen studied under Clement in Alexandria.
pairs.nazianzen|jerome: Jerome studied under Gregory of Nazianzus in Constantinople and called him his teacher.
